title: Why Republicans Are Winning Swing Voters

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分采访内容，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily, today.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》，今日报道。

sentences.en: With nearly two weeks to go before elections that will determine which party controls the House and
sentences.zh: 距离决定哪个党派控制众议院和

sentences.en: Senate, a major new poll from the Times has found that swing voters who had backed Democrats are suddenly switching sides and supporting Republicans.
sentences.zh: 参议院的选举还有不到两周时间，《纽约时报》的一项重要新民调发现，此前支持民主党的摇摆选民正突然倒戈，转而支持共和党。

sentences.en: My colleague, Nate Cohn, explains why that is and what it will likely mean on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 我的同事内特·科恩将解释其中的原因，以及这对选举日可能意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月20日，星期四。

sentences.en: Nate?
sentences.zh: 内特？

sentences.en: Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I mean, okay.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，还行吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I have the sense every election season that this is your game time.
sentences.zh: 每个选举季我都有种感觉，这是你的“比赛时间”。

sentences.en: This is basically Christmas for your little corner of the world.
sentences.zh: 对你这一小方天地来说，这基本上就是圣诞节。

sentences.en: Well, Christmas, you know, I think typically brings a little bit more happiness than the election can bring.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我觉得圣诞节通常比选举能带来的快乐要多一点。

sentences.en: Unless you want to count the polls as a gift.
sentences.zh: 除非你把民调结果当成礼物。

sentences.en: I do enjoy the polls, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我确实很喜欢民调，不得不说。

sentences.en: I do too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: So we wanted to talk to you right now because the political winds have changed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在想找你聊聊，因为政治风向已经变了。

sentences.en: The last time you came on the show over the summer, you told us that according to multiple
sentences.zh: 上次你夏天来节目时，你告诉我们根据多项

sentences.en: polls, including polls conducted by the Times, Democrats were doing surprisingly well, despite
sentences.zh: 民调，包括《纽约时报》进行的民调，民主党的表现出人意料地好，尽管

sentences.en: longstanding rules in American politics which say that the party that controls the White House is supposed to get crushed in midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 美国政治中有一条长期存在的规则，即控制白宫的政党在中期选举中通常会惨败。

sentences.en: Somehow, Democrats were poised to potentially avoid that fate, according to the polls.
sentences.zh: 根据民调，民主党人似乎有望避免这种命运。

sentences.en: What did the latest poll tell us about what happened to that summer of relative Democratic love?
sentences.zh: 最新的民调告诉我们，那个相对属于民主党的“夏天”发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: Well, if our last poll found a summer of Democratic love, then I think our poll suggests that the electorate's summer fling with the Democrats is coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果说我们上次的民调发现了一个属于民主党的夏天，那么我认为这次的民调表明，选民与民主党之间的“夏日恋情”即将结束。

sentences.en: We show the Republicans now taking the lead on this poll question called the generic congressional ballot.
sentences.zh: 我们显示共和党现在在“国会选举通用投票”这一民调问题上处于领先地位。

sentences.en: It's a little complicated, but it just asks voters whether they want to vote for a Democrat or Republican for
sentences.zh: 这有点复杂，但它只是询问选民在他们所在选区的

sentences.en: Congress in their district.
sentences.zh: 国会选举中是想投票给民主党还是共和党。

sentences.en: And in this poll, we show the Republicans leading by three percentage points by that measure.
sentences.zh: 在这项民调中，我们显示共和党在该指标上领先三个百分点。

sentences.en: In our last poll, just a month ago, we show the Democrats up by one point.
sentences.zh: 而在一个月前的上次民调中，我们显示民主党领先一个百分点。

sentences.en: So that's a four-point swing towards the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 所以这相当于向共和党倾斜了四个百分点。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Can you put a four-point swing into some perspective for those of us who don't live in the polling world?
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些不生活在民调世界里的人来说，你能把这四个百分点的波动放在一个背景下解释一下吗？

sentences.en: I would describe that as a modest but meaningful swing.
sentences.zh: 我会将其描述为一种适度但有意义的波动。

sentences.en: It's a large enough number where you don't just assume it's just random noise necessarily.
sentences.zh: 这个数字足够大，你不能仅仅认为它只是随机噪声。

sentences.en: And importantly, in this case, it's also backed by other evidence.
sentences.zh: 而且重要的是，在这种情况下，它也得到了其他证据的支持。

sentences.en: We have a lot of different data points.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多不同的数据点。

sentences.en: We see the Republicans gaining in a lot of key Senate races, a number of important House districts, including House
sentences.zh: 我们看到共和党在许多关键的参议院竞选中取得进展，在一些重要的众议院选区也是如此，包括那些

sentences.en: districts where the Democrats probably shouldn't even be in trouble.
sentences.zh: 民主党本不该陷入困境的选区。

sentences.en: And you just put it all together, and I think we've got a clear picture here.
sentences.zh: 把这些放在一起看，我认为我们已经得到了一个清晰的图景。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when we think about a four-point swing and what these midterms are fundamentally all about, right, which is control of the United States House, the United States Senate,
sentences.zh: 当我们思考这四个百分点的波动以及中期选举的根本意义时，也就是对美国众议院和参议院的控制权，

sentences.en: how does a four-point swing help us understand Republican chances in these elections?
sentences.zh: 这四个百分点的波动如何帮助我们理解共和党在这些选举中的胜算？

sentences.en: I think it's the difference between whether the Democrats are favored in the Senate and whether the Senate's a toss-up.
sentences.zh: 我认为这决定了民主党在参议院是处于优势，还是参议院的选情变得难以预料。

sentences.en: And it's the difference between whether the Democrats can at least dream about the House and whether the House is just going Republican.
sentences.zh: 这也决定了民主党是还能对众议院抱有幻想，还是众议院将彻底倒向共和党。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So how does this latest poll help us understand why there was this meaningful swing from Democrats to Republicans in a pretty short period of time since the summer?
sentences.zh: 那么，这项最新民调如何帮助我们理解为什么自夏天以来，在如此短的时间内，选民从民主党转向共和党出现了这种有意义的波动？

sentences.en: You know, a lot of polls that we conduct, it can be hard to tell the story of why things changed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们进行的很多民调，很难说清楚事情为什么会发生变化。

sentences.en: There are cross-cutting indicators, or you see a weird number and you wonder whether it could be real.
sentences.zh: 会有相互矛盾的指标，或者你看到一个奇怪的数字，会怀疑它是否真实。

sentences.en: But I think this poll actually tells a really simple and unusually clear story.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这次民调实际上讲述了一个非常简单且异常清晰的故事。

sentences.en: And it shows that the issues that voters are focused on right now are very different from the ones they were focused on over the summer when we last chatted.
sentences.zh: 它表明选民目前关注的问题与我们上次聊天时夏天关注的问题大不相同。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's worth trying to remember what it was like when we last did this poll in early July.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，值得回顾一下我们上次在7月初进行这项民调时的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah, please.
sentences.zh: 好的，请讲。

sentences.en: It was just two weeks after the Dobbs decision overturned Roe versus Wade.
sentences.zh: 那是在多布斯案推翻罗诉韦德案裁决后的两周。

sentences.en: I mean, you can remember how much media coverage there was about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以回想一下当时媒体对此有多少报道。

sentences.en: There were protests, new state trigger bans were going into effect every day.
sentences.zh: 到处是抗议活动，新的州级触发禁令每天都在生效。

sentences.en: It was at the very forefront of the public conversation and understandably slow.
sentences.zh: 它处于公众讨论的最前沿，而且可以理解的是，热度持续不减。

sentences.en: I mean, that's going to be something our grandkids are going to learn about in the history books.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这将是我们孙辈在历史书中会学到的内容。

sentences.en: It was a really significant historic event.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重大的历史事件。

sentences.en: And the other thing we were talking about over the summer was gun violence.
sentences.zh: 我们夏天讨论的另一件事是枪支暴力。

sentences.en: In just a three-month period, we had the shooting in Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 在短短三个月内，我们经历了布法罗枪击案。

sentences.en: There was the Uvalde shooting.
sentences.zh: 还有尤瓦尔迪枪击案。

sentences.en: And then on July 4th, there was that shooting at a parade in Highland Park, Illinois.
sentences.zh: 然后在7月4日，伊利诺伊州海兰帕克市的游行中又发生了枪击事件。

sentences.en: Congress was moving on gun control legislation at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时国会正在推进枪支管制立法。

sentences.en: So gun control is an issue and gun violence as a problem were also really high on the minds of voters at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以枪支管制作为一个议题，枪支暴力作为一个问题，在当时也确实占据了选民心头的重要位置。

sentences.en: And like abortion, a sudden focus on gun violence and gun control is pretty good for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 就像堕胎一样，对枪支暴力和枪支管制的突然关注对民主党来说相当有利。

sentences.en: You know, a majority of voters tends to favor the Democratic position on, say, an assault gun ban and supports abortion being mostly legal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大多数选民倾向于支持民主党在诸如攻击性武器禁令上的立场，并支持堕胎在很大程度上合法化。

sentences.en: And then the final category is democracy.
sentences.zh: 最后一个类别是民主。

sentences.en: As you may recall, over the summer, the January 6th hearings were a nationally televised, almost weekly event.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，在夏天，1月6日国会山骚乱听证会是一个全国性电视转播的、几乎每周一次的事件。

sentences.en: And the January 6th hearings served to elevate democracy.
sentences.zh: 1月6日的听证会起到了提升“民主”议题的作用。

sentences.en: And in particular, the Stop the Steal movement and election denial and President Trump's conduct in the minds of voters.
sentences.zh: 特别是“停止窃选”运动、选举否认主义以及特朗普总统的行为，在选民心中变得突出。

sentences.en: Every time there was a January 6th hearing, there's a whole set of stories afterwards.
sentences.zh: 每次有1月6日的听证会，随后都会有一连串的相关报道。

sentences.en: And it became an important part of the national conversation.
sentences.zh: 它成为了全国对话的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: So that too was a good issue for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以这对民主党来说也是一个有利的议题。

sentences.en: So for all those reasons, this sudden prominence of three very meaty issues that aid the Democrats on a generic ballot, the end of summer 2022 is a kind of high watermark when it
sentences.zh: 所以基于所有这些原因，这三个对民主党在通用投票中非常有利的重大议题突然凸显，2022年夏末是民主党在进入中期选举前的民调高点。

sentences.en: comes to polling for the Democratic Party heading into these midterMs. Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But what our poll shows is that those three issues have really started to fade away.
sentences.zh: 但我们的民调显示，这三个议题确实已经开始淡出。

sentences.en: And they have been replaced by a series of issues that are much more favorable to the Republicans, the economy, and even immigration and crime.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是一系列对共和党更有利的议题：经济，甚至还有移民和犯罪。

sentences.en: If I can put a number on that, Michael, you know, when we last talked, 26% of voters just
sentences.zh: 如果我能用数字来量化这一点，迈克尔，你知道，我们上次谈话时，26%的选民

sentences.en: volunteered that democracy, abortion, or gun violence was the most important issue faced in the country.
sentences.zh: 主动表示民主、堕胎或枪支暴力是国家面临的最重要问题。

sentences.en: And this poll, it's down to 14.
sentences.zh: 而在这次民调中，这一比例下降到了14%。

sentences.en: So it's basically in half.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上减半了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: On the other end of the ledger, the proportion saying that either the economy, crime and immigration is the most important issue went from 38% when we last talked to 52%.
sentences.zh: 在另一端，认为经济、犯罪和移民是首要问题的比例从我们上次谈话时的38%上升到了52%。

sentences.en: So a majority of voters in this poll are now focused on one of these issues that favors the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 因此，这项民调中大多数选民现在关注的是这些有利于共和党的议题之一。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: And as is the case with how we can tell a pretty clear story for why voters were focused on, you know, abortion and democracy and guns over the
sentences.zh: 正如我们能清楚地讲述为什么选民在夏天关注堕胎、民主和枪支问题一样，

sentences.en: summer, I think we can tell a similarly clear story about why they're focused on this different set of issues now.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们也能同样清楚地解释为什么他们现在关注这一组不同的议题。

sentences.en: Well, let's take these three issues that you just brought up as favorable to Republicans,
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈你刚才提到的对共和党有利的三个议题，

sentences.en: the economy, crime, immigration, and talk about how they end up becoming such a powerful force that explains this switch since the summer from Democrats to Republicans.
sentences.zh: 经济、犯罪、移民，并讨论它们是如何成为一股强大的力量，解释了自夏天以来选民从民主党转向共和党的这种转变。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So, I mean, let's start with the economy.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们从经济开始吧。

sentences.en: The official economic numbers confirmed what American households already know.
sentences.zh: 官方的经济数据证实了美国家庭早已知晓的事实。

sentences.en: Prices continue to rise in September.
sentences.zh: 9月份物价继续上涨。

sentences.en: According to...
sentences.zh: 根据……

sentences.en: Over the last month, the economic picture has, you know, gotten quite a bit worse.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一个月里，经济状况确实变得糟糕多了。

sentences.en: Food up 11.2% year over year.
sentences.zh: 食品价格同比上涨11.2%。

sentences.en: Rent up 7.2%.
sentences.zh: 租金上涨7.2%。

sentences.en: The largest increase since 1982.
sentences.zh: 这是自1982年以来的最大涨幅。

sentences.en: The inflation news has turned from okay to quite a bit worse.
sentences.zh: 通胀消息已经从“还行”变成了“糟糕得多”。

sentences.en: The Dow Jones sank about 630 points.
sentences.zh: 道琼斯指数下跌了约630点。

sentences.en: The Nasdaq...
sentences.zh: 纳斯达克……

sentences.en: The stock market has fallen a lot.
sentences.zh: 股市已经大幅下跌。

sentences.en: Gas prices have been dropping throughout the summer, but recent news from overseas sent them right back up again.
sentences.zh: 汽油价格在整个夏天一直在下降，但最近来自海外的消息又让它们回升了。

sentences.en: Gas prices bottomed out in early September and began to increase.
sentences.zh: 汽油价格在9月初触底，随后开始上涨。

sentences.en: And so it is no surprise to me that the share of people focused on the economy has gone from 35 to 45%.
sentences.zh: 所以，关注经济的人群比例从35%上升到45%，我一点也不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are a lot of people who, you know, are struggling day to day with rising costs or, you know, looking at their 401ks.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有很多人每天都在为不断上涨的成本而挣扎，或者看着他们的401k退休金账户发愁。

sentences.en: So you have both this combination of abortion being farther in the rearview mirror, and that steady drumbeat of
sentences.zh: 所以你既有堕胎议题渐行渐远、相关报道的持续热度消退的因素，

sentences.en: stories on that topic fading, but also a new set of stories about the economy that people are living every day.
sentences.zh: 也有人们每天都在亲身经历的关于经济的新闻报道。

sentences.en: I mean, and there's no way around it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是无法回避的。

sentences.en: You know, the president is always held accountable for the state of the economy, whether the president deserves it or not.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论总统是否应该负责，他总是要为经济状况承担责任。

sentences.en: And in this case, the Republicans have, you know, a credible pitch that Democratic policies like the Recovery Act contributed to the inflation by overstimulating the economy.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，共和党有一个可信的论点，即民主党的政策（如《复苏法案》）通过过度刺激经济加剧了通货膨胀。

sentences.en: So this is a tough issue for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以这对民主党来说是一个棘手的议题。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Let's turn to crime and immigration as issues that favor Republicans.
sentences.zh: 让我们转向犯罪和移民这两个有利于共和党的议题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You know, I think crime and immigration are both really interesting because they're both
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为犯罪和移民都非常有趣，因为它们都是

sentences.en: issues where I don't think it's as much the news that's helped put that issue at the forefront of voters' minds, but Republican strategy.
sentences.zh: 我不认为主要是新闻报道将这些议题推向了选民关注的前沿，而是共和党的策略。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Turn now to immigration, the showdown playing out right here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在转向移民问题，今晚在美国上演的对峙，

sentences.en: tonight, far from the U.S.-Mexico border.
sentences.zh: 远离美墨边境。

sentences.en: You know, start on immigration.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从移民问题开始。

sentences.en: Remember that a couple of weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 记得几周前吗？

sentences.en: Florida's Governor Ron DeSantis flying roughly 50 migrants to Martha's
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯将大约50名移民空运到了马萨诸塞州的

sentences.en: Vineyard, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 马萨葡萄园岛。

sentences.en: Governor DeSantis shipped migrants to Martha's Vineyard.

sentences.en: Nate, once these issues that had been favorable to Democrats are replaced by issues more favorable to Republicans, what kinds of voters make this switch, according to
sentences.zh: 内特，一旦这些对民主党有利的议题被对共和党更有利的议题所取代，根据民调，

sentences.en: the poll, from favoring Democrats on the generic ballot to suddenly favoring Republicans and getting us to this four-point swing?
sentences.zh: 什么样的选民会发生这种转变，从在普选票上支持民主党突然转向支持共和党，并导致了我们看到的这四个百分点的波动？

sentences.en: Well, the simplest answer is the people who support the Democratic position on issues like abortion or guns, but who are potentially sympathetic to the Republicans on
sentences.zh: 嗯，最简单的答案是那些在堕胎或枪支等问题上支持民主党立场，但可能在

sentences.en: other issues like the economy or crime or immigration.
sentences.zh: 经济、犯罪或移民等其他问题上对共和党抱有同情的选民。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are millions of people out there who hold these sort of conflicting views.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有数以百万计的人持有这种相互矛盾的观点。

sentences.en: Republicans who are pro-choice, for instance, or an independent voter who is anti-immigration and pro-abortion.
sentences.zh: 例如，支持堕胎权的共和党人，或者反对移民但支持堕胎权的独立选民。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, voters are complicated.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，选民是很复杂的。

sentences.en: Most voters are complicated.
sentences.zh: 大多数选民都很复杂。

sentences.en: The people who are ideologically consistent who agree with their party on everything, even if they're strong partisans, are the minority.
sentences.zh: 那些在意识形态上保持一致，在所有问题上都同意自己党派观点的人，即使他们是坚定的党派支持者，也只是少数。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, specifically, let's talk about the groups of voters who make this switch.
sentences.zh: 那么，具体来说，让我们谈谈那些发生转变的选民群体。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd have to start with women.
sentences.zh: 是的，我得从女性开始说起。

sentences.en: You know, women have long leaned towards the Democrats in no small part because of issues like abortion and gun policy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，女性长期以来倾向于民主党，很大程度上是因为堕胎和枪支政策等问题。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But many women are also susceptible to caring about the economy.
sentences.zh: 但许多女性也容易关心经济问题。

sentences.en: Many women are also deeply concerned about crime.
sentences.zh: 许多女性也对犯罪深感担忧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, indeed, our poll does show the Republicans making pretty meaningful gains among women over the summer.
sentences.zh: 而且，确实，我们的民调显示共和党在夏季期间在女性群体中取得了相当显著的增长。

sentences.en: Now, I should say that when you get to polls of gender or any subgroup for that matter, polls become a little less reliable.
sentences.zh: 现在，我必须说，当你进行性别或任何子群体的民调时，民调的可靠性会降低一些。

sentences.en: Our poll is just not designed to be a perfect representation of subgroups.
sentences.zh: 我们的民调设计初衷并非为了完美代表各个子群体。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's room to wonder about just how much the Republicans have gained.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，对于共和党到底增长了多少，还有怀疑的空间。

sentences.en: But clearly, in terms of just the direction that our poll shows, it shows the Republicans doing better among women than they had done previously.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，就我们民调显示的趋势而言，它表明共和党在女性中的表现比以前更好。

sentences.en: And it makes sense if you believe that the electorate has gone from focusing on a set of issues where women are especially likely
sentences.zh: 如果你认为选民已经从关注那些女性特别倾向于支持民主党立场的议题，转向了那些

sentences.en: to back the Democratic position to those where maybe there's a little bit less of an advantage for
sentences.zh: 民主党在女性中优势可能稍小一些的议题，那么这就说得通了。

sentences.en: Democrats among women.
sentences.zh: 民主党在女性中。

sentences.en: But we tend to think of abortion as somewhat unique and core to voters' identity, especially women voters.
sentences.zh: 但我们倾向于认为堕胎在某种程度上是独特的，是选民身份的核心，尤其是女性选民。

sentences.en: And so what you're describing is a phenomenon in which maybe that assumption is just kind of wrong?
sentences.zh: 所以你所描述的是一种现象，即那种假设可能有点错误？

sentences.en: Well, I think there are a lot of voters out there who care deeply about abortion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为有很多选民非常关心堕胎问题。

sentences.en: You could even call them single-issue voters if you would.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，甚至可以称他们为单一议题选民。

sentences.en: But, you know, the middle 50% of the electorate, I don't think I would put in that category.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，中间那50%的选民，我不认为我会把他们归入那一类。

sentences.en: They may care about abortion a lot, but it's one of many important issues to them.
sentences.zh: 他们可能非常关心堕胎，但这只是他们众多重要议题中的一个。

sentences.en: Just as one anecdote, you know, in our poll, only 5% of voters volunteer that abortion is the most important problem in the country right now, including less than 10% of women.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，你知道，在我们的民调中，只有5%的选民自发提到堕胎是目前国内最重要的问题，其中女性不到10%。

sentences.en: It's only 1% of men.
sentences.zh: 男性只有1%。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这很多。

sentences.en: You know, this is an open-ended question, and that was the first thing they named, 1 in 20 people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个开放式问题，这是他们提到的第一件事，20个人里有1个。

sentences.en: But 19 in 20 people think there's something else more important out there, even if they care deeply about the issue.
sentences.zh: 但20个人里有19个认为还有其他更重要的事情，即使他们非常关心这个问题。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So who else, besides women, swung in a meaningful way in this poll towards Republicans?
sentences.zh: 那么除了女性之外，还有谁在这项民调中向共和党发生了显著的转变？

sentences.en: I guess I would say maybe working-class voters is a second category.
sentences.zh: 我想我会说是工薪阶层选民，这是第二个类别。

sentences.en: I mean, usually pollsters define working-class voters as people without a college degree.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通常民调机构将工薪阶层选民定义为没有大学学位的人。

sentences.en: For this conversation, you know, I guess I would slightly, you know, redefine this to really mean people who care about pocketbook
sentences.zh: 对于这次谈话，你知道，我想我会稍微重新定义一下，真正指那些关心钱袋子

sentences.en: economic issues, whether it's because they're more economically vulnerable or just because they care more about their finances than, you know, ideological questions.
sentences.zh: 经济问题的人，无论是因为他们在经济上更脆弱，还是仅仅因为他们比意识形态问题更关心自己的财务状况。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In our poll, for instance, you know, 49% of people without a degree listed the economy or inflation as the most important issue compared to 37% of college graduates.
sentences.zh: 例如，在我们的民调中，你知道，49%没有学位的人将经济或通货膨胀列为最重要的问题，而大学毕业生中这一比例为37%。

sentences.en: So as the economy becomes more important, it does tend to land more among working-class voters.
sentences.zh: 所以随着经济变得越来越重要，它确实倾向于更多地落在工薪阶层选民身上。

sentences.en: But again, you know, that's going to hit anybody who just privileges the economy in their thinking.
sentences.zh: 但同样，你知道，这会影响任何在思考中优先考虑经济的人。

sentences.en: It can be a relatively affluent person thinking about retirement, looking at their 401k crashing, right?
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个相对富裕的人在考虑退休，看着他们的401k账户缩水，对吧？

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So that's the economy, which has a very unique power over voters of all kinds in elections.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是经济，它在选举中对各类选民都有着非常独特的影响力。

sentences.en: Who did this poll find seems to have moved from
sentences.zh: 这项民调发现谁似乎因为移民和犯罪的具体议题而从

sentences.en: Democratic to Republican because of the specific issues of immigration and crime?
sentences.zh: 民主党转向了共和党？

sentences.en: Is that knowable?
sentences.zh: 这能知道吗？

sentences.en: That one's tough.
sentences.zh: 那个很难说。

sentences.en: I mean, the number of people who are citing that as the most important issue is fairly small.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，将此列为最重要议题的人数相当少。

sentences.en: We're only talking about, I think, a combined 8% on those two issues.
sentences.zh: 我想我们谈论的只是这两个议题加起来8%的人。

sentences.en: And that's in no small part because many Republicans right now who may care deeply about crime and immigration are prioritizing the economy over that.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为许多目前可能非常关心犯罪和移民的共和党人，正在将经济置于这些问题之上。

sentences.en: But, you know, I can say that those are issues as well where working-class voters, and especially white working-class voters, are much more likely to say it's the
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我可以说这些也是工薪阶层选民，尤其是白人工薪阶层选民，比白人大学毕业生更有可能将其称为

sentences.en: most important problem than white college graduates.
sentences.zh: 最重要问题的问题。

sentences.en: You know, in the case of crime, I mean, only like
sentences.zh: 你知道，就犯罪而言，我的意思是，只有大约

sentences.en: 1% of college-educated voters in our poll think crime is the biggest problem.
sentences.zh: 我们民调中1%受过大学教育的选民认为犯罪是最大的问题。

sentences.en: You know, it just doesn't register for people who can, you know, live in communities with lower crime rates and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于那些可以生活在犯罪率较低社区的人来说，这根本不算什么。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So the same working-class voter who seems inclined to think that the economy is a big problem
sentences.zh: 所以，那个倾向于认为经济是他们生活中大问题的工薪阶层选民，

sentences.en: in their lives is similarly inclined to think crime and immigration are a problem in their lives.
sentences.zh: 同样倾向于认为犯罪和移民是他们生活中的问题。

sentences.en: And all three of those issues, as you have explained to us very well, favor Republicans.
sentences.zh: 正如你向我们解释得非常清楚的那样，这三个议题都对共和党有利。

sentences.en: Yeah, and we have Republicans winning by a very large margin among voters who select one of those issues.
sentences.zh: 是的，在选择这些议题之一的选民中，共和党以非常大的优势获胜。

sentences.en: So if you get a 10-point increase in the number of Americans who are listing one of them, that can pay off in big ways, and at least in our poll it does.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能让将其中一个议题列为首位的美国人增加10个百分点，那就能带来巨大的回报，至少在我们的民调中是这样。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Nate, I'm curious what happened to the issue of democracy and threats to democracy.
sentences.zh: 内特，我很好奇民主和对民主的威胁这些议题发生了什么。

sentences.en: We've talked about every other issue but that when we try to understand this switch.
sentences.zh: 当我们试图理解这种转变时，我们谈论了除此以外的所有议题。

sentences.en: Because it might be true that the January 6th hearings have faded away and they have become less frequent.
sentences.zh: 因为1月6日的听证会可能确实已经淡出人们的视野，变得不那么频繁了。

sentences.en: And we've talked about how the news cycle really matters when it comes to the prominence of these issues.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到过新闻周期在这些议题的突出程度方面确实很重要。

sentences.en: But election denialism is a very big part of this midterm election.
sentences.zh: 但选举否认主义是这次期中选举中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: We know that because hundreds of Republican candidates are running on the false claim that
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点，因为数百名共和党候选人都在竞选中宣扬虚假主张，称

sentences.en: Biden didn't really win the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 拜登并没有真正赢得2020年大选。

sentences.en: And so it's hard to imagine that issue has just kind of faded out of people's lives.
sentences.zh: 所以很难想象这个议题就这样从人们的生活中消失了。

sentences.en: So what does the poll find about what happened to democracy?
sentences.zh: 那么民调发现民主议题发生了什么？

sentences.en: And to the degree that it is still important to people, which party it favors?
sentences.zh: 在它对人们仍然重要的程度上，它对哪个党派有利？

sentences.en: Well, the poll found that a lot of people are concerned about democracy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，民调发现很多人关心民主。

sentences.en: I mean, more than 70% of voters said they thought democracy was under threat, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，超过70%的选民表示他们认为民主受到威胁，对吧？

sentences.en: So that would seem to imply that it ought to be a very big issue in this election.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎意味着它应该是这次选举中一个非常大的议题。

sentences.en: The catch, though, is that many of the people who say democracy is under threat don't really mean what you were just talking about, Michael.
sentences.zh: 然而，问题在于，许多说民主受到威胁的人，并不真的是指你刚才谈到的那些，迈克尔。

sentences.en: When we ask them open-ended, why is democracy under threat?
sentences.zh: 当我们问他们开放式问题，为什么民主受到威胁时？

sentences.en: They're not talking about stop the steal for the most part.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，他们谈论的不是“停止窃选”。

sentences.en: They're not talking about election denialism.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的不是选举否认主义。

sentences.en: They're not talking about January 6th.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的不是1月6日事件。

sentences.en: They're more likely to talk about corruption.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能谈论腐败。

sentences.en: They're more likely to talk about polarization.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能谈论两极分化。

sentences.en: They're more likely to list something that just has nothing to do with democracy, too, like inflation or something.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能列出一些与民主完全无关的事情，比如通货膨胀之类的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So while many voters, you know, will tell a pollster they're concerned about democracy, only a small number of them are conceiving of that word and that topic
sentences.zh: 所以虽然许多选民会告诉民调人员他们关心民主，但只有少数人是以你刚才提到的那种方式

sentences.en: in the same way that you just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 来理解这个词和这个话题的。

sentences.en: I should note, though, Michael, the people who do take the view of democracy that you just did, who say the threat to democracy is stop the steal and right-wing
sentences.zh: 不过我应该指出，迈克尔，那些确实持有你刚才那种民主观的人，那些说对民主的威胁是“停止窃选”、右翼

sentences.en: authoritarianism and election denial and so on, the people who did tell us that, for them, democracy is the most important issue.
sentences.zh: 威权主义和选举否认等等的人，那些确实告诉我们这些的人，对他们来说，民主是最重要的议题。

sentences.en: They're just only 17% of the electorate.
sentences.zh: 他们只占选民的17%。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: For the group that has adopted the understanding of the threat to democracy that you did, it's a huge issue, and most voters just don't see it that way.
sentences.zh: 对于那些采纳了你那种对民主威胁理解的群体来说，这是一个巨大的议题，但大多数选民并不这么看。

sentences.en: So when we look back at the summer, Nate, where we started this conversation, and how Democrats were
sentences.zh: 所以当我们回顾夏天，内特，我们开始这次谈话的时候，以及民主党人当时

sentences.en: doing unexpectedly well, I'm curious, should we think of that as basically a historical anomaly, right?
sentences.zh: 表现得好得出人意料，我很好奇，我们是否应该将其视为一个历史性的反常现象，对吧？

sentences.en: A violation of the normal political rules around how a party in power is going to perform in midterms?
sentences.zh: 是对执政党在期中选举中表现如何的正常政治规则的违背？

sentences.en: And therefore, we should treat this latest poll, where Republicans are doing better, as a return to normalcy.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们是否应该将这份共和党表现更好的最新民调视为回归常态？

sentences.en: Or should we view this change as a very rare opportunity that Democrats had over the summer, but somehow squandered?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该将这种变化视为民主党在夏天拥有但以某种方式浪费掉的非常罕见的机会？

sentences.en: I'm curious how you think about it.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇你是怎么想的。

sentences.en: Well, we'll see the final result in a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几周后我们就会看到最终结果。

sentences.en: But if we stipulate for a second that, you know, the Republicans go on and win the national vote by three points, like you might guess from our generic
sentences.zh: 但如果我们暂时设定，你知道，共和党人继续以三个百分点的优势赢得全国投票，就像你可能从我们的普选票

sentences.en: ballot number, you know, I think we would say that this was something more like a return to normal.
sentences.zh: 数字中猜测的那样，你知道，我想我们会说这更像是回归常态。

sentences.en: After all, what happened over the summer was historic.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，夏天发生的事情是历史性的。

sentences.en: You know, the court's decision in
sentences.zh: 你知道，法院在

sentences.en: Dobbs is, again, it's going to be taught in the history books.
sentences.zh: 多布斯案中的裁决，再说一次，它将被写进历史书里。

sentences.en: Is there something that Democrats could have done to try and keep abortion in the news down the stretch and keep immigration and crime out?
sentences.zh: 民主党人有没有什么办法可以在最后阶段让堕胎问题留在新闻中，并让移民和犯罪问题远离新闻？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: You know, maybe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许吧。

sentences.en: I do think that Democrats are doing everything they can to keep it in the news.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为民主党正在尽一切努力让它留在新闻中。

sentences.en: I have to say that I was back home for a baseball game, watched the
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我回老家看了一场棒球比赛，看了

sentences.en: Mariners lose in 18 innings.
sentences.zh: 水手队在18局比赛中输掉比赛。

sentences.en: And the Democratic ads were constantly about abortion.
sentences.zh: 而民主党的广告一直在谈论堕胎。

sentences.en: So I think the party's trying to bring back the summer.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为该党正在努力带回夏天的势头。

sentences.en: But, you know, airing political ads and talking about it on the campaign stump is not the same as it being legitimate breaking news that's dominating the national conversation.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，播放政治广告和在竞选演讲中谈论它，与它成为主导全国对话的合法突发新闻是两码事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Joe Biden is releasing more oil from the strategic petroleum reserve today and trying to bring down oil costs.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登今天正在从战略石油储备中释放更多石油，并试图降低石油成本。

sentences.en: Maybe that'll help down the stretch to at least dull the economic issues a little bit to give a little more breathing room to their efforts to return focus on abortion.
sentences.zh: 也许这会有助于在最后阶段至少稍微缓解经济问题，从而为他们重新关注堕胎的努力提供更多的喘息空间。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to predict what will happen over the next few weeks.
sentences.zh: 很难预测未来几周会发生什么。

sentences.en: And we have definitely seen, you know, those, quote, October surprises in the paSt. But the reality is it's really hard for the Democrats to recreate what they had over the summer.
sentences.zh: 我们确实见过，你知道，那些所谓的“十月惊奇”在过去。但现实是，民主党真的很难重现他们在夏天所拥有的那种优势。

sentences.en: They can try and recreate it with advertisements the same way the Republicans, you know, have tried to bring back issues like crime and immigration.
sentences.zh: 他们可以尝试用广告来重塑这种局面，就像共和党人试图重提犯罪和移民等议题一样。

sentences.en: But that's not the same as recreating a truly historic moment when the whole national conversation is focused on an issue where Democrats have the advantage.
sentences.zh: 但这与重现一个真正的历史性时刻不同，当时全国上下的谈话焦点都集中在民主党占优势的议题上。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，内特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是今天你需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, Russia declared martial law in four regions of Ukraine that it has illegally annexed
sentences.zh: 周三，俄罗斯宣布在其非法吞并的乌克兰四个地区实施戒严，

sentences.en: but does not fully control, a move that will allow Russian leaders to impose even tighter restrictions on the people who live there.
sentences.zh: 尽管俄罗斯并未完全控制这些地区，但此举将允许俄罗斯领导人对当地居民实施更严格的限制。

sentences.en: The decision appears to be a response to Russian military setbacks that have allowed Ukrainian forces to advance further and further into the annexed territory.
sentences.zh: 这一决定似乎是对俄军挫败的回应，这些挫败使得乌克兰军队能够进一步深入被吞并的领土。

sentences.en: And in a bad sign for inflation, two of the world's largest companies, Nestle and
sentences.zh: 对于通胀来说，这是一个坏消息，全球两家最大的公司雀巢和

sentences.en: Procter & Gamble, both acknowledged on Wednesday that they have raised prices throughout the last few
sentences.zh: 宝洁都在周三承认，它们在过去几个月里提高了价格，

sentences.en: months and plan to continue to do so to maintain their profits despite lower consumer demand.
sentences.zh: 并计划继续涨价以维持利润，尽管消费需求有所下降。

sentences.en: Nestle, for instance, which makes products like Cheerios and Kit Kat bars, said it had raised prices by nearly 10 percent during the third quarter of the year.
sentences.zh: 例如，生产脆谷乐和奇巧巧克力棒等产品的雀巢公司表示，在今年第三季度，其价格上涨了近10%。

sentences.en: Those price increases undermine efforts by government officials to lower inflation and are expected to keep consumer prices higher for a longer period of time.
sentences.zh: 这些价格上涨削弱了政府官员降低通胀的努力，预计将使消费价格在更长的时间内保持高位。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗谢尔·班贾和悉尼·哈珀制作。

sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威兰斯和丽莎·周编辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和

sentences.en: Alicia Ba Etoop and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 艾丽西亚·巴·埃图普的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由吉姆·布伦伯格和本·

sentences.en: Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 兰斯福德（来自Wonderly）创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》我们将为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要全黑的睡眠环境吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否喝得烂醉才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是指他们对光线有什么要求，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
